title: Phase 3: signal ingestion
description: Needs planning: the signal→tick funnel (Worker commits tick JSON via GitHub contents API, DO inbox as conflict buffer); webhook-mode Telegram with draft-tick triage and Create/Dispatch buttons; GitHub issue ingestion behind the tk label consent boundary; generic webhook sources registered in .tick/config.md; external_ref dedup everywhere; trace IDs from the front door (D20).
notes:
2026-08-19 15:30 - [human] Scope expanded 2026-08-19 by human decision: Telegram/GitHub rungs of the UC1b command vocabulary (D21) are Phase 3. See docs/design/cloud-factory.md UC1b.
2026-08-19 21:38 - [human] Scope (human question, 2026-08-19): ONE Telegram bot/chat now serves MANY projects, since one factory serves many projects. Machine routing is already unambiguous — RunRoom is per-project (idFromName(project+epic)), question ids are unique-by-registration (afj), and inline-keyboard callback data carries the question id, so a BUTTON answer always resolves exactly one question in exactly one project. Two gaps remain:

1. LEGIBILITY. kv2 routes by project on the API side (FactoryChannel.projectPath) but nothing composes the project into the Telegram message text. Two repos in one chat produce indistinguishable questions. Every gate message, report and completion must name project + epic + tick. Cheap, and it is what makes a shared chat usable at all.

2. FREE-TEXT ANSWERS ARE AMBIGUOUS, and this is a correctness issue rather than a nicety. Rules to implement, fail-closed:
   - A Telegram reply-to a specific question message resolves THAT question. Deterministic; prefer it.
   - Bare text with exactly ONE open question across all projects resolves it.
   - Bare text with TWO OR MORE open questions must REFUSE and list the candidates. Never guess: an approval carries human provenance into the verdict guard, so a wrong guess attributes the operator's approval to another project's gate.

3. UPGRADE PATH, optional: a Telegram supergroup in forum mode gives one topic per project via message_thread_id — one bot, one chat, natively separate threads, replies scoped to their topic. The rules above are what make a shared chat work WITHOUT it, so treat topics as an enhancement rather than a prerequisite.
